texts: 8   DAgger: trained on its own states
Does a model that is fine-tuned on the states IT reaches make its tactical decisions survive its own motion?
tier T1-kin = self-action OPEN loop  |  NOT closed loop: the cameras are the human's recorded frames, nothing re-renders the scene

During the fine-tune a fraction p = 0.1
of the training samples is REPLACED by
a state the model itself reached: its
own rolled-out ego state (speed,
history, odometry, route countdown) at
2 s or 4 s into a T1-kin rollout.

The states come from a bank of the
starting checkpoint's own rollouts over
the TRAINING clips (306,566 windows per
seed; 75.6 % / 76.9 % of the windows
have an eligible own state, seed 0 /
seed 1).

The label stays the HUMAN's: the 6 s
future and the tactical labels at the
route point the own state matches.  The
images stay the human's logged frames:
nothing is re-rendered.

The same fine-tune with p = 0: same
init (the M2b checkpoint), 3,000 steps,
learning rate 1e-4, same data, same
seed.

It separates 'trained on its own
states' from 'trained for more steps':
the effect of the lever is DAG minus
DAG-0, never DAG against the old
checkpoint.

Both arms, two training seeds (s0, s1),
are run at T1-kin on the 141 evaluation
episodes (2,399 windows) and read by a
rule committed before the runs
(PREREG_V8F_DAGGER).

Seven windows chosen by a rule fixed
before any chapter-8 frame was rendered
(next card).

For each: DAG and DAG-0 side by side,
each on its OWN motion, at the replan
ticks (+0, +2, +4 s).  S: route
checkpoints, 30 / 50 / 80 m ahead.  T:
the lateral and longitudinal decision
(head argmax) against the label.  O:
the path it executes, against the
human's.

Then the distribution over all 2,399
windows, the pre-registered T-head
rows, and the guards.  Where DAG is
worse, the caption says so.

Estimator: paired episode-cluster bootstrap, B = 2,000, 141 episodes, 2,399 windows, DAG - DAG-0 per training seed (answers 'another draw of EPISODES' only); another TRAINING run
is answered by the two seeds and the replicate floor RF; the planner is deterministic.

Baseline: DAG-0 is the same fine-tune without the lever, not the state of the art; no external benchmark is shown.  Evidence class of every number in this chapter: MEASURED (ours),
from the float64 T1-kin dumps, the per-tick files, and the pre-registered read data/DAG_READ.json.

8  DAgger: which windows are shown, and why
rule fixed BEFORE any chapter-8 frame was rendered  |  SELECTION_V5.md, select_scenes5.py (it reads g and cl of the two seed-0 runs, nothing else)

THE RULE   (sha256 ee759319dfafa149...)

delta_w = ADE6(DAG, seed 0) - ADE6(DAG-0, seed 0) of window w,
T1-kin, causal, m = 10 (negative: DAG closer to the human's path),
over the 2,399 windows in the dump order.
1. For each GT stratum (JUNCTION, CURVE, NO-TURN;
window_strata_eval141.npz, defined from the human's labels) sort the
stratum's windows by (|delta_w|, grid row) ascending and take
position (n - 1) // 2: the lower median of |delta|, the typical size
of change in that stratum.
2. WORST: the window with the largest delta_w over all 2,399 windows
(ties: lowest grid row).
3. Three DRAWS: numpy.random.default_rng(20261027).choice(n_cand, 3,
replace=False) over the windows (dump order) with GT mean speed >= 5
m/s that are not already chosen by 1 or 2.
No window is swapped or dropped for how it looks; a window where DAG
is worse stays in.
The seven windows, in the order shown
#  tag      stratum    eval win      clip  t (s)    m/s  delta s0 (m)

delta = ADE6(DAG) - ADE6(DAG-0) of the window at seed 0, T1-kin (negative: DAG
closer to the human's path): the quantity the rule sorts by, printed here for
the record.  Draw positions in the candidate list: 1390, 1882, 415.  Seed 1 is
shown beside in every window and was not used to choose.
Why a rule, and why these windows are NOT a sample of the typical window

A median window shows the TYPICAL size of the change in its stratum, whichever way it goes, so a window where DAG is worse is as likely to be picked
as one where it is better; the WORST window is the largest increase over all 2,399 windows, kept because a video that shows only wins is not evidence;
the three draws are random among windows that move (at least 5 m/s).  A window is an example; the distribution card and the result cards are the
evidence.

Strata (from the human's labels): JUNCTION 298 windows, CURVE 140, NO-TURN 1,961 (2,399 in all).  Candidates for the three draws: 1,908.  The median
windows are one JUNCTION and one CURVE and one NO-TURN window; the WORST window and the three draws all fall in NO-TURN, by far the largest stratum.

What the rule cannot do: it cannot make seven windows a sample.  The distribution card shows all 2,399, and the two result cards carry the decision-
grade rows.

Each window is shown with DAG on the left and DAG-0 on the right, both at training seed 0 in the picture, both reading the SAME logged camera frames,
each running on its OWN executed motion.  The per-window ADE6 of both seeds is in the table and the caption at the end of each window.

and the replicate floor RF; the planner is deterministic.
